lyrics:
[Intro: clean guitar arpeggio, soft organ, room tone]

[Verse 1: deep male baritone, murmured]
Sheets of paper, curled and yellow
Came down easy, one by one
Crayon horses, purple fellows
A house, a tree, a square of sun

[Verse 2: bass and brushed drums enter]
Now the wall's a field of pinholes
Eighteen years of little stars
I could fill them, I could paint it
I just stand here where you are

[Chorus: band rises, voice opening]
All I've got is thumbtack holes
Where your drawings were
Every one a day you handed me
And I said, "That's nice," and stirred
I'd give anything to look again
All I've got is thumbtack holes

[Verse 3: voice rougher, electric guitar in]
Your room still smells like your shampoo
There's a sock behind the door
Your mother's on the phone with you
I can't. I'll call. I'm on the floor.

[Chorus: full band, voice howling]
All I've got is thumbtack holes
Where your drawings were
Every one a day you handed me
And I said, "That's nice," and stirred
I'd give anything to look again
All I've got is thumbtack holes

[Bridge: band crashing, voice at its limit]
I know you're fine! I know it's right!
I know this is the thing we raised you for!
I know! I know!

[Outro: band drops to piano and guitar, wordless vocal, crowd joining]
Doo doo doo, doo doo doo doo
Doo doo doo, doo doo doo doo
(I'm not going to paint it)
Doo doo doo, doo doo doo doo
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 76 BPM, 4/4, E minor. Slow, heavy and aching, with a long, loose build.

VOICE: Male baritone, deep and trembling. He murmurs the verses almost under his breath, opens up in the first chorus and howls the second chorus and bridge with his voice breaking. The outro is a wordless melody sung softly, joined by other voices.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar arpeggio, Hammond organ, piano, bass, a drum kit played with brushes and then sticks, a second distorted guitar with long feedback notes, a slide guitar.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro. 0:20 Verse 1. 0:52 Verse 2. 1:24 Chorus 1. 2:00 Verse 3. 2:32 Chorus 2. 3:08 Bridge. 3:36 Outro, wordless melody building and fading to 4:58.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1990s Seattle rock: warm, live and unpolished, a band in a room, vocal raw and loud.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The murmured '(I'm not going to paint it)' under the outro at 4:20.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original mourns a lover with a young man's intensity. A father's version of that grief is quieter and comes with an argument against itself: he knows this is what was supposed to happen.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Numb, remembering, breaking, letting the wall stay.
